comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts a DRG 80 gripper’s opening-stop screw to 90°, locks the setting with a jam nut, and verifies retained opening through repeated cold-lever cycles. PR 2245 instead removes a loose screwdriver from a control box, shuts and latches its cover, and safely switches on a test supply.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests coaxial driver and thin-wrench seating, simultaneous screw counterholding and nut tightening without disturbing an angular setting, tool regrasping/withdrawal, and articulated functional verification. PR 2245 tests loose-tool extraction and placement, hinged-cover closure, catch engagement, rocker actuation, and safe sequencing. They share only generic grasping, tool handling, and mechanism actuation.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate scores measured opening accuracy, locknut/second-nut retention, one then three repeatable close-open cycles, limited stop drift, and released-tool clearance, with loss conditions for missing hardware, dropped tools, fixture displacement, or invalid motion. PR 2245 scores the screwdriver removed, resting and released on the table, the cover shut and latched, safe switch-on, and gripper clearance; unsafe energization permanently forces zero. Both available PR 2245 spec versions state the same substantive rubric.
comparison.reason: The tested ability is meaningfully different: preserving a calibrated mechanical stop while applying coupled countertorque and proving adjustment retention is not tested by enclosure housekeeping, latching, and safe re-energization. Different industrial settings alone are not the basis for distinction.
